paragraphs.text: For nearly a decade now, Merebeth has been a self-employed pet transport specialist. Her pet transport job was born of the financial crisis (危机) in the late 2000s. The downturn hit the real estate (房地产) firm where she had worked for ten years as an office manager. The firm went broke and left her looking for a new job. One day, while driving near her home, she saw a dog wandering on the road, clearly lost. She took it home, and her sister in Denver agreed to take it. This was a loving home for sure, but 1,600 miles away. It didn’t take long for Merebeth to decide to drive the dog there herself. It was her first road trip to her new job.

Merebeth’s pet delivery service also satisfies her wanderlust. It has taken her to every state in the US except Montana, Washington and Oregon, she says proudly. If she wants to visit a new place, she will simply find a pet with transport needs there. She travels in all weathers. She has driven through 55 mph winds in Wyoming, heavy flooding and storms in Alabama and total whiteout conditions in Kansas.

This wanderlust is inherited from her father, she says. He moved their family from Canada to California when she was one year old, because he wanted them to explore a new place together. As soon as she graduated from high school she left home to live on Catalina Island off the Californian coast, away from her parents, where she enjoyed a life of sailing and off-road biking.

It turns out that pet transporting pays quite well at about 30,000 per year before tax. She doesn’t work in summer, as it would be unpleasantly hot for the animals in the car, even with air conditioning. As autumn comes, she gets restless – the same old wanderlust returning. It’s a call she must handle alone, though. Merebeth says, “When I’m on the road, I’m just in my own world. I’ve always been independent-spirited and I just feel strongly that I mush help animals.”

The United States rose to global power on the strength of its technology, and the lifeblood of that technology has long been electricity. By providing long-distance communication and energy, electricity created the modern world. Yet properly understood, the age of electricity is merely the second stage in the age of steam, which began a century earlier.

“It is curious that no one has put together a history of both the steam and electric revolutions,” writes Maury Klein in his book The Power Makers: Steam, Electricity, and the Men Who Invented Modern America. Klein, a noted historian of technology, spins a narrative (叙述) so lively that at times it reads like a novel.

The story begins in the last years of the 18th century in Scotland, where Watt perfected “the machine that changed the world”. Klein writes, “America did not invent the steam engine, but once they grasped its possibilities they put it to more uses than anyone else.”

Meanwhile, over the course of 19th century, electricity went from mere curiosity to a basic necessity. Morse invented a code for sending messages over an electromagnetic circuit. Bell then gave the telegraph a voice. Edison perfected an incandescent bulb (白炽灯泡) that brought electric light into the American home.

Most importantly, Edison realized that success depended on mass electrification, which he showed in New York City. With help from Tesla, Westinghouse’s firm developed a system using alternating current (交流电) , which soon became the major form of power delivery.

To frame his story, Klein creates the character of Ned, a fictional witness to the progress brought about by the steams and electric revolutions in America during one man’s lifetime. It’s a technique that helps turn a long narrative into an interesting one.

The benefits of regular exercise are well documented but there’s a new bonus to add to the ever-growing list. New research found that middle-aged women who were physically fit could be nearly 90 percent less likely to develop dementia (失智症) in later life – and if they did, it came on a decade later than less sporty women.

Lead researcher Dr Helena Ho¨rder, of the University of Gothenburg in Sweden, said, “These findings are exciting because it’s possible that improving people’s cardiovascular (心血管的) fitness in middle age could delay or even prevent them from developing dementia.”

For the study, 191 women with an average age of 50 took a bicycle exercise test until they were tired out to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity. The average peak workload was measured at 103 watts.

A total of 40 women met the criteria for a high fitness level with a capacity of 120 watts or higher, while 92 women were in the medium fitness category. A total of 59 were of low fitness level, with a peak workload of 80 watts or less, or having their tests stopped because of health problems.

These women were then tested for dementia six times over the following four decades. During that time, 44 of the women developed dementia. Five percent of the highly fit women developed dementia, compared to 25 percent of the women with medium fitness and 32 percent of the women with low fitness.

“However, this study does not show cause and effect between cardiovascular fitness and dementia, it only shows an association,” said Ho¨rder. “More research is needed to see if improved fitness could have a positive effect on the risk of dementia and also to look at when during a lifetime a high fitness level is most important.” She also admitted that a relatively small number of women were studied, all of whom were from Sweden, so the results might not be applicable to other groups.

Kim Cobb, a professor at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta, is one of a small but growing minority of academics __56__are cutting back on their air travel because of climate change. Travelling to conferences, lectures, workshops, and the like – frequently by plane – __57__ (view) as important for scientists to get together and exchange information. When Dr. Henderson was assigning (指定) project mates for his psychology class, I secretly hoped he would pair me with my best friend or at least a classmate I could have some fun with. Above all, I hoped he wouldn’t assign me to work with the fiercely competitive and extremely serious fellow who always wore dark clothes and apparently had a personality to match. As fate (命运) would have it, Dr. Henderson very deliberately matched everyone in class and announced that I would be working with the one person in class I wanted to avoid.

I went up to my new teammate and introduced myself. He looked at me as though I weren’t there. I felt he treated me as though I would hold him back and probably make him fail to get an A in the course. He wasn’t mean or abusive; he just gave me the impression he could do whatever project we dreamed up better if he did it alone.
Needless to say, I didn’t look forward to an entire term of being brushed off, but I tried to make the best of it and didn’t say anything for fear that I would make things worse.

The project required each team to develop a hypothesis (假说) , set up an experiment to test the hypothesis, do the statistical analysis and present the findings. Whatever grade the team received would be shared by both students.

When my teammate and I met to discuss our project, I was uneasy. Here was this challenging student who had a reputation for single-mindedness and good grades – the exact opposite of me. I actually wanted to drop the class at one point, but stopped short because I didn’t want to give him the satisfaction of my chickening out. I decided to stick to it no matter what.
After long discussions we somehow agreed to do a study on the psychological well-being of teenagers. I wasn’t sure what it meant exactly, but at least we had a topic.

group-zj-2022-jan-reading-a.overview: 记叙文。讲述 Merebeth 由地产公司办公室经理转行成为自雇宠物运输专员的经历，以及她对四处漫游（wanderlust）的热爱、这份热爱的来源（父亲）和她独立自主的工作状态。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按‘起因—现状—溯源—回报与心境’的逻辑展开：先讲转行契机，再写宠物运输如何满足其漫游欲，接着追溯漫游欲来自父亲，最后说明收入、淡季安排及她独来独往的内心世界。

paragraphs.summary: 金融危机使 Merebeth 所在的地产公司倒闭、她被迫另谋出路；一次偶遇救助流浪狗并亲自驱车 1600 英里送往丹佛，成为她新职业的开端。
paragraphs.function: 交代主人公转行的起因和宠物运输职业的缘起。

paragraphs.summary: 宠物运输工作满足了她的漫游欲，足迹几乎遍及全美各州；她不惧各种恶劣天气，穿越大风、洪水风暴和暴雪。
paragraphs.function: 说明这份工作如何满足她四处游历的渴望，并以 wanderlust 一词承上启下。

paragraphs.summary: 她的漫游欲遗传自父亲：父亲在她一岁时举家从加拿大迁往加州以探索新地方；高中毕业后她便离家独居 Catalina 岛，过着航海与越野骑行的生活。
paragraphs.function: 追溯 wanderlust 的来源，刻画其独立天性的成长背景。

paragraphs.summary: 宠物运输税前年收入约 3 万；夏天因车内对动物太热而不工作；入秋后她又会因漫游欲而坐不住；这是一份她必须独自面对的召唤，她始终独来独往、独立自主。
paragraphs.function: 交代收入、淡季安排，并揭示她独立、独行的内心世界，收束全文。

group-zj-2022-jan-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇书评，评介历史学家 Maury Klein 的著作 The Power Makers: Steam, Electricity, and the Men Who Invented Modern America。文章先指出电力是美国崛起的命脉，再说明电力时代实为蒸汽时代的第二阶段，随后按时间梳理书中讲述的蒸汽机与电力革命的发展，最后点评作者用虚构人物 Ned 串联叙事的写作手法。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先立论（电力支撑美国崛起、电力时代是蒸汽时代的延续），再引入并介绍 Klein 及其著作，接着按时间顺序复述书中蒸汽机与电力革命的关键人物与事件，最后评价作者塑造虚构见证者 Ned 的叙事技巧。

paragraphs.summary: 美国凭技术崛起，电力是技术的命脉并创造了现代世界；但准确地说，电力时代只是早一个世纪开始的蒸汽时代的第二阶段。
paragraphs.function: 提出全文核心观点，确立蒸汽时代与电力时代之间的承接关系，为评介的著作主题做铺垫。

paragraphs.summary: 引用 Klein 在书中的话——尚无人把蒸汽与电力两场革命合写成史；并介绍 Klein 是知名技术史学家，其叙述生动得有时读来像小说。
paragraphs.function: 引入被评介的著作及其作者，点明该书填补的空白与生动的叙述风格。

paragraphs.summary: 故事始于18世纪末苏格兰，Watt 完善了“改变世界的机器”；美国虽未发明蒸汽机，却把它用到了比谁都多的用途上。
paragraphs.function: 复述书中蒸汽革命的开端，承接蒸汽时代主题。

paragraphs.summary: 19世纪间电力从新奇之物变为必需品：Morse 发明电报码，Bell 让电报有了“声音”，Edison 完善白炽灯泡把电光带进美国家庭。
paragraphs.function: 复述书中电力革命的关键人物与发明，展现电力地位的演进。

paragraphs.summary: 最重要的是 Edison 意识到成功取决于大规模电气化，并在纽约市加以展示；借助 Tesla，Westinghouse 公司开发出交流电系统，很快成为主要供电方式。
paragraphs.function: 续述电力革命的高潮，突出大规模电气化与交流电的意义。

paragraphs.summary: 为搭建叙事框架，Klein 虚构了人物 Ned，让他作为一个人一生中见证美国蒸汽与电力革命进步的见证者；这一手法把冗长的叙述变得有趣。
paragraphs.function: 评点作者的叙事技巧，呼应第二段“读来像小说”的评价，收束全文。

group-zj-2022-jan-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇科普说明文，报道一项瑞典研究的发现：中年时心血管体能良好的女性日后患失智症的风险显著更低，即使患病也会推迟约十年。文章按照「引出新发现—专家评价—研究方法与分组—结果数据—研究局限」的顺序展开。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先用「锻炼益处清单又添一项」引出新研究结论，再借首席研究员之口评价其意义，随后说明研究的实验方法和体能分组，列出各组失智发病率数据，最后由研究员指出研究只显示相关性而非因果，并坦承样本局限。

paragraphs.summary: 引出新研究：中年体能好的女性患失智症的概率可低近九成，即使患病也推迟约十年。
paragraphs.function: 引入话题并点明核心发现

paragraphs.summary: 首席研究员 Hörder 评价该发现令人振奋，认为提升中年心血管体能或可延缓甚至预防失智。
paragraphs.function: 借专家之口阐释发现的意义

paragraphs.summary: 介绍研究方法：191 名平均年龄 50 岁的女性骑车测试至力竭，以测量最大心血管能力，平均峰值负荷 103 瓦。
paragraphs.function: 说明研究对象与测量方法

paragraphs.summary: 按峰值负荷把女性分为高（120 瓦及以上，40 人）、中（92 人）、低（80 瓦及以下或因健康问题中止，59 人）三个体能等级。
paragraphs.function: 说明体能分组标准与人数

paragraphs.summary: 随后四十年间六次检测失智，44 人发病；高体能组发病率 5%，中体能组 25%，低体能组 32%。
paragraphs.function: 呈现随访结果与各组发病率数据

paragraphs.summary: 研究员指出该研究只显示相关性而非因果，需更多研究，并坦承样本量小且仅来自瑞典，结论未必适用于其他人群。
paragraphs.function: 指出研究的局限性与谨慎结论

q-zj-2022-jan-022.questionFocus: 考查第二段 wanderlust 一词的词义推测，需结合该段对其旅行行为的具体描述及上下文复现。

optionAnalysis.label: B

q-zj-2022-jan-024.questionFocus: 考查对 Klein 关于“电力时代”这一观点的理解，需定位作者转述 Klein 视角处的细节。

trapEvidence.anchor: 早一个世纪开始的是蒸汽时代

q-zj-2022-jan-025.questionFocus: 考查对虚构人物 Ned 的推断，需结合末段对 Ned 角色设定的描述进行合理推理。
q-zj-2022-jan-025.stemTranslationZh: 关于 Ned 可以推断出什么？

trapEvidence.anchor: 纽约市是 Edison 展示电气化之地

locationParaphrases.targetText: a fictional witness to the progress brought about by the steams and electric revolutions in America during one man’s lifetime

q-zj-2022-jan-026.questionFocus: 考查文章体裁/文本类型的判断，需综合全文“评介一本著作”的写作目的与内容来判定。
q-zj-2022-jan-026.stemTranslationZh: 这篇文章属于什么类型？

q-zj-2022-jan-027.questionFocus: 考查对首段「不断增长的清单」所指内容的细节理解，需要从指代语境中确定清单的实质内容。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 运动型女性相比男性的优势。

trap.claim: Advantages of sporty women over men.
trap.explanation: 原文未提及男性，也未做任何「女性优于男性」的比较，全文只在女性内部比较不同体能水平，属无中生有。

locationParaphrases.targetText: The benefits of regular exercise are well documented
locationParaphrases.note: 正确项 Positive effects of doing exercises 与原文 The benefits of regular exercise 同义替换，benefits 即 positive effects，清单即「锻炼益处」之列表。

q-zj-2022-jan-028.questionFocus: 考查对研究方法的细节理解，需定位研究者让受试者骑车的目的。
q-zj-2022-jan-028.stemTranslationZh: 研究人员为什么要求这些女性做自行车运动？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了预测她们的最大心率。

trap.sourceQuote: to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity
trap.optionText: To predict their maximum heart rate.
trap.explanation: 原文测量的是「峰值心血管能力（peak cardiovascular capacity）」，并非「最大心率（maximum heart rate）」。该项利用 peak/maximum 的相近，把测量对象错配成心率，属对象错配。

trapEvidence.quote: to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了评估她们的心血管能力。

evidence.quote: took a bicycle exercise test until they were tired out to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity
evidence.anchor: bicycle test ... to measure ... cardiovascular capacity

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了改变她们的锻炼习惯。

trap.claim: To change their habit of working out.
trap.explanation: 原文骑车测试只为测量心血管能力，从未提及要改变受试者的锻炼习惯，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为了查出她们潜在的健康问题。

trap.sourceText: having their tests stopped because of health problems
trap.optionText: To detect their potential health problems.
trap.relationNote: 原文 health problems 出现在第四段，是指部分人因健康问题而中止测试、被归入低体能组，并非骑车测试的「目的」。该项借用原词 health problems 制造干扰，把分组时的一个附带情形偷换成实验目的。

trapEvidence.quote: having their tests stopped because of health problems
trapEvidence.anchor: health problems = reason tests stopped, not the purpose

locationParaphrases.targetText: to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity
locationParaphrases.note: 正确项 assess 与原文 measure 同义替换，cardiovascular capacity 原词对应，目的状语 to measure... 即骑车测试的目的。

q-zj-2022-jan-029.questionFocus: 考查对 Hörder 研究的整体细节判断，需结合随访时长、研究目的与研究局限逐项核对。
q-zj-2022-jan-029.stemTranslationZh: 关于 Hörder 博士的研究，我们可以得知什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它旨在找到治疗失智症的方法。

trap.claim: It aimed to find a cure for dementia.
trap.explanation: 原文称该研究只显示体能与失智之间的「相关性」，目的是观察关联，并未以「寻找治疗失智的方法（a cure）」为目标，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 数据收集是一个漫长的过程。

evidence.quote: These women were then tested for dementia six times over the following four decades.
evidence.anchor: tested six times over four decades

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 一些参与者中途退出了研究。

trap.sourceText: having their tests stopped because of health problems
trap.optionText: Some participants withdrew from it.
trap.relationNote: 原文说部分人因健康问题被「中止测试（tests stopped）」，指的是体能测试当场停止并据此归入低体能组，与「参与者退出整项研究（withdrew）」不是一回事。该项借「停止/退出」的近义联想制造干扰。

trapEvidence.quote: having their tests stopped because of health problems

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 研究结果远不能令人满意。

trap.sourceQuote: These findings are exciting because it’s possible that improving people’s cardiovascular (心血管的) fitness in middle age could delay or even prevent them from developing dementia.
trap.optionText: The results were far from satisfactory.
trap.explanation: 研究员评价结果「令人振奋（exciting）」，态度积极；该项却说结果「远不能令人满意」，与原文情感倾向相反，属黑白颠倒。文末提到的样本局限是研究的客观限制，而非对结果质量的负面评价。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Data collection was a lengthy process
locationParaphrases.targetText: These women were then tested for dementia six times over the following four decades.
locationParaphrases.note: 正确项 a lengthy process 由原文 six times over the following four decades（四十年间检测六次）推断而来，长达数十年的反复检测即「数据收集过程漫长」。

q-zj-2022-jan-030.questionFocus: 考查标题概括能力，需选出最能覆盖全文核心结论且范围恰当的标题。
q-zj-2022-jan-030.stemTranslationZh: 下列哪一项是本文最佳标题？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 越来越多女性通过锻炼来预防失智症。

trap.claim: More Women Are Exercising to Prevent Dementia
trap.explanation: 全文报道的是一项关于「体能与失智关联」的研究发现，并未说「越来越多女性正在为预防失智而锻炼」这一社会趋势，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 中年女性需要做更多锻炼。

trap.sourceQuote: However, this study does not show cause and effect between cardiovascular fitness and dementia, it only shows an association
trap.optionText: Middle-Aged Women Need to Do More Exercise
trap.explanation: 原文强调研究只显示相关性、并不构成因果，故无法据此直接得出「中年女性需要多锻炼」这一带建议性、强断言的结论。该标题把谨慎的相关发现夸大为行动主张，属范围偷换（夸大）。

trapEvidence.quote: this study does not show cause and effect between cardiovascular fitness and dementia, it only shows an association
trapEvidence.anchor: only an association, not a directive

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 体能好的女性患失智症的可能性更小。

evidence.quote: New research found that middle-aged women who were physically fit could be nearly 90 percent less likely to develop dementia (失智症) in later life
evidence.anchor: physically fit women ... less likely to develop dementia

evidence.quote: Five percent of the highly fit women developed dementia, compared to 25 percent of the women with medium fitness and 32 percent of the women with low fitness.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 骑车能改善女性的心血管体能。

trap.sourceQuote: took a bicycle exercise test until they were tired out to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity
trap.sourceEntity: a bicycle exercise test (to measure capacity)
trap.optionText: Biking Improves Women's Cardiovascular Fitness
trap.explanation: 文中骑车只是用来「测量」心血管能力的测试手段，并非用来「改善（improves）」体能。该标题把测量工具错配为提升体能的方法，且只涉及局部细节，无法概括全文，属对象错配。

trapEvidence.quote: took a bicycle exercise test until they were tired out to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity
trapEvidence.anchor: bicycle = measuring tool, not the booster

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Fit Women Are Less Likely to Develop Dementia
locationParaphrases.targetText: middle-aged women who were physically fit could be nearly 90 percent less likely to develop dementia
locationParaphrases.note: 正确标题 Fit Women Are Less Likely to Develop Dementia 直接概括首段核心句 physically fit ... less likely to develop dementia，并由第五段各体能组发病率数据（5% vs 25%/32%）佐证，覆盖全文主旨。
